craft_notes: Sthāyin: doubt dissolving (vilīne). Abhinavagupta frame: vyabhicāri-dissolution (śaṅkā melting) staged as the rupture — piled reasonings one breath, melted cloud the next; śānta-close enacted (row 12: falling cadence on ‘darkness’, long vowels, still image — the metaphysics of the ending, not decoration). Rows: 1 (spṛśatu late — ‘let me touch’ before the simile), 2 (yukti-pracaya-racana-unmārjana compound unpacked down the line-break; bank: Ingalls moon-drops unpacking), 8 (vowel arc melts→blazes), 12 (śānta-fall). Close: ‘the sun that conquers darkness’ — darkness last, conquered. Rejected: merging two sources — killed: UNC keeps guru-word and scripture two; cutting sun-simile — killed: vibhāva does the settling; ‘lifts’ for vilīne — killed: melts, not lifts. Read aloud: BY the GU-ru’s WORD … WHEN the DOUBT-cloud MELTS … LIKE the SUN that CON-quers DARK-ness.

lines: By the guru’s word — whose force wipes clean the heaped fabric of reasonings —
and by assurance, fittingly told, regarding scripture:
when the doubt-cloud melts, let me touch the feet of the Lord,
whose splendor blazes in the heart’s sky like the sun that conquers darkness.

notes: guru’s word + assurance kept as two sources; one-twofold-source reading open
